korea.title: Flag of the Republic of Korea (Taegeukgi)

colors.note: Background; represents peace, purity, and the Korean people's traditional love of white (baekui minjok, 'white-clad folk').
Upper half of the taegeuk; represents positive cosmic forces (yang), the sun, and warmth.
Lower half of the taegeuk; represents negative cosmic forces (yin), the moon, and coolness.
Four trigrams (geon, gon, gam, ri); represent the four classical elements — heaven, earth, water, and fire.

desc:
- A white field with a red-and-blue taegeuk (yin-yang symbol) at the centre, surrounded by four black trigrams from the I Ching
- The taegeuk represents the balance of cosmic forces
- The four trigrams — geon (heaven), gon (earth), gam (water), and ri (fire) — symbolise the principles of movement and harmony
- Colour specifications were standardized by Presidential ordinance on 25 October 1997 and codified in the National Flag Law of July 2007
- **Construction:** a white field with the taegeuk centred
- The taegeuk circle's diameter is half the hoist
- Four black trigrams are placed in the four corners, each at a distance from the centre equal to the flag's quarter-width
- The red (upper) and blue (lower) halves of the taegeuk are S-curved
trivia:
- The trigrams are from the I Ching (Book of Changes); the taegeuk (circle) represents balance between cosmic forces
- The red and blue are complementary colours representing the harmony of Yin and Yang
- South Korea adopted this flag in 1945; the design is based on ancient Korean symbolism

korea-dprk.title: Flag of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea

colors.note: Broad central stripe; represents the revolutionary spirit and the blood shed in the struggle for independence.
Top and bottom stripes; represent sovereignty, peace, and friendship.
Narrow stripes and the disc; represent purity and the cultural heritage of the Korean people.

desc:
- A broad red central stripe bordered by thin white and then blue stripes, with a white disc containing a red five-pointed star on the hoist side
- The red star on the white disc symbolises the revolutionary traditions and the guiding ideology of Juche, established by Kim Il-sung
- The blue stripes stand for sovereignty, peace, and friendship
- Adopted on 8 September 1948 when the Democratic People's Republic of Korea was proclaimed, replacing the traditional taegeukgi
- **Construction:** five horizontal bands — blue, white, red (central, wider), white, blue — in ratio 1:0.5:3:0.5:1
- A white disc on the hoist half of the red stripe contains a red five-pointed star
- Ratio 1:2
trivia:
- North Korea's flag was designed to deliberately reject the traditional Korean taegeuk symbol
- The white circle represents purity; the red represents revolution and socialism
- North Korea adopted this flag in 1948 to emphasize its communist ideology separate from the South
